lines.trans: My mother is extra sensitive about recycling and exhaust fumes—her nickname is actually the Yeouido Busybody…
A busybody? See, this is why a person must behave nicely every day—yet once a situation hits, my temper flares up!
Hey, how come you came into work today anyway? Afraid of taking leave because you are the youngest?
Instead, I plan to leave early later and stop by your new apartment—the window installer is coming, and I can drop off boxes too.
I am super grateful and all, yet am I really allowed to work you like this?
It is something I do because I enjoy it.
Oh, you enjoy this kind of stuff—moving house, interior decorating, and all that?

Really? Then can you help me out tomorrow? It is Music Bank's mid-year special, so we have tons of stages!

Do you really mean that? Not the feeling-sorry part—the part right before it where I am your favorite…
You did not know? Out of all my juniors, I like you the best!

examples.text: 우리 가위바위보 해서 서로 짐 들어 주기 할까요?
examples.trans: Shall we play rock-paper-scissors to carry each other's bags?

출근하다.gloss: to go to work, to commute to the office

meanings.en: to go to work / arrive at the office
meanings.note: Used for commuting to one's workplace

examples.trans: I went to work early this morning.

examples.text: 지하철로 출근하는 데 삼십 분 걸려요.
examples.trans: It takes thirty minutes to commute by subway.

I worked hard to after leaving work yesterday too.

examples.trans: There is a special broadcast tonight.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 평소처럼 필름이 끊겨 있는 게 선배님이 바라는 해피엔딩이신 거죠?
examples.trans: So having his memory blacked out like usual is the happy ending you are hoping for, right?
Here the word for 'like usual' is key.
